# [JEP 238: Multi-Release JAR Files](https://openjdk.org/jeps/238)

A simple example demonstrating how Multi-Release JAR Files can enable named
modules for Java 1.8 JARs. Although Java 1.8 does not support
`module-info.java`, this can be achieved using Multi-Release JAR Files.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 11](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java11)

- [Oracle Java 8](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java8)

## Run the example

1. Build the application using Java 11

   Verify that Java 11 is the default version of Java.

   ```shell
   java --version
   ```

   The default Java version

   ```
   java 11.0.32.1 2026-08-18 LTS
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment 18.9 (build 11.0.32.1+1-LTS-5)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM 18.9 (build 11.0.32.1+1-LTS-5, mixed mode)
   ```

   Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) List the generated classes

   ```shell
   tree --dirsfirst --sort=name './target/classes'
   ```

   The application classes

   ```
   ./target/classes
   ├── demo
   │   ├── Demo.class
   │   ├── Describable.class
   │   └── Main.class
   └── META-INF
       └── versions
           └── 11
               ├── demo
               │   └── Demo.class
               └── module-info.class

   6 directories, 5 files
   ```

   Please note that a `versions` directory exists under `META-INF`, containing
   the classes for the corresponding Java version.

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file

   ```
   ./target/libs
   └── multi-release-jar-file-one-module.jar

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

   (*Optional*) List the JAR file contents

   ```shell
   jar --list --file='./target/libs/multi-release-jar-file-one-module.jar' | sort
   ```

   The application JAR file contents

   ```
   demo/
   demo/Demo.class
   demo/Describable.class
   demo/Main.class
   META-INF/
   META-INF/MANIFEST.MF
   META-INF/maven/
   META-INF/maven/demo/
   META-INF/maven/demo/multi-release-jar-file-one-module/
   META-INF/maven/demo/multi-release-jar-file-one-module/pom.properties
   META-INF/maven/demo/multi-release-jar-file-one-module/pom.xml
   META-INF/versions/
   META-INF/versions/11/
   META-INF/versions/11/demo/
   META-INF/versions/11/demo/Demo.class
   META-INF/versions/11/module-info.class
   ```

3. Describe the JAR file

   Describe the `multi-release-jar-file-one-module.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/multi-release-jar-file-one-module.jar'
   ```

   Unfortunately, this will not work as expected because it is a multi-release
   JAR file and the `--release` option was not specified.

   ```
   releases: 11

   No root module descriptor, specify --release
   ```

   Specify the release version using the `--release` option. Note that the order
   of the parameters is important; if changed, the command will not function
   correctly.

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/multi-release-jar-file-one-module.jar' --release 11
   ```

   The multi-release-jar-file-one-module module description when executed with
   Java 11

   ```
   releases: 11

   demo@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/multi-release-jar-file-one-module.jar/!META-INF/versions/11/module-info.class
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo
   main-class demo.Main
   ```

4. Verify the class bytecode version

   Print the `Main.class` bytecode version

   ```shell
   javap -v './target/classes/demo/Main.class' | grep major
   ```

   The `Main.class` bytecode version.

   ```
     major version: 52
   ```

   All classes within the `src/main/java` source folder are compiled to Java 1.8
   (major version: 52).

   Print the `module-info.class` byte code version

   ```shell
   javap -v './target/classes/META-INF/versions/11/module-info.class' | grep major
   ```

   The `module-info.class` bytecode version.

   ```
     major version: 55
   ```

   All classes within the `src/main/java11` source folder are compiled to
   Java 11 (major version: 55).

5. Run the application

   The JAR file is both backward compatible and future-proof and can run with
   both Java 1.8 or newer and can take advantage of newer Java features, such as
   Java Modules. The application simply prints the Java version.

   Assuming that the environment variable `JAVA_1_8_HOME` contains the path to
   the Java 1.8 home directory.

   ```shell
   "${JAVA_1_8_HOME}/bin/java" -version
   ```

   The Java 8 version

   ```
   java version "1.8.0_503"
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.8.0_503-b01)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.503-b01, mixed mode)
   ```

   Run the application using Java 1.8

   ```shell
   "${JAVA_1_8_HOME}/bin/java" -jar './target/libs/multi-release-jar-file-one-module.jar'
   ```

   The application will run and prints

   ```
   JEP 238: Multi-Release JAR Files
   Java version: 1.8.0_503
   From the 'java' source dir
   ```

   Run the application using Java 11, or above

   ```shell
   java --version
   ```

   The default Java version

   ```
   java 11.0.32.1 2026-08-18 LTS
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment 18.9 (build 11.0.32.1+1-LTS-5)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM 18.9 (build 11.0.32.1+1-LTS-5, mixed mode)
   ```

   Run the application using the module path

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/libs' --module demo
   ```

   The application will run and prints

   ```
   JEP 238: Multi-Release JAR Files
   Java version: 11.0.32.1
   From the 'java11' source dir
   ```
